Just finished Seveneves by Neal Stephenson

I also finished it the other day. [Warning: this post contains plenty of spoilers]

Like many people, I powered through the first two thirds quickly, and then lost interest for a week or two once the final section began. So much lengthy tell-don't-show of how the world works, with no actual character (Kath Two barely qualifies as a character) or plot for quite some time. Luckily it all picks up again, and reaches a reasonably satisfying ending, but there was a bit of a slog in the middle there.

I quite liked a lot of it. In a novel that tries to do so much, it seems unfair of me to complain about the stuff that it doesn't do, but I do feel like it could have spent a little less time being Kerbal Space Program: The Book (there were exact numbers on some of the delta-Vs, for crap's sake) and a bit more time developing some of the characters in the first part. What was really the difference between Dinah and Ivy, anyway? Who was Moira again? These people are gonna be important later, they should be developed better. The only character I really felt I knew was Doob, but that's hardly fair, because he's just you-know-who with a different name.

In the final section, there's some equal disappointments. We know from Anathem and The Diamond Age that Neal Stephenson is interested in how cultures might change under different circumstances, but here he doesn't seem to bother. Fifty centuries pass, and culture stays astonishingly similar. (For fuck's sake, they watch scenes from The Epic all the time just for fun?) The Digger culture changes, but not in as interesting a way as it might have. The Pingers seemed like they were going to be genuinely interesting, but we don't get to find out anything about them.

Anyway, I don't regret the time I spent reading it (unlike Reamde) so it goes on my shelf of "slightly disappointing Neal Stephenson books post-Cryptonomicon".

I really enjoyed your thoughts on this book, thanks for sharing them!

Ah. See, what you disliked, I loved. But I understand your point of view!

I loved the deltavees, I agree on the whole Doob thing.

I really enjoyed the final section. I think the Epic playing all the time says a lot about the people in charge, and how they strove to keep the same system in place, which would make sense for a culture derived from 8 people living on a space station! I really enjoyed it. It will take a place on my top shelf.

I look forward to reading more Neal Stephenson. This was my first book by him.
